01 / The Founder Bottleneck

As the company grows,
the way you run it has to change.

The founder holds an enormous amount of context, relationships and decision-making that doesn’t automatically transfer as the business grows.

It doesn’t simply disappear into the team either. More people, priorities and dependencies create a different kind of complexity, and more of it finds its way back to you.

01Priorities

Everything feels important.

02Decisions

Too many still need you.

03Context

Too much of what the business needs to know still lives with you.

04Execution

You become the connection between teams.

05 Attention

The company consumes the
attention you need to lead it.

The company you're building needs your judgement,
not your involvement in everything required to run it.

You don't need to let go of the company.
You need to stop holding all of it.

Founder leverage isn't about being less involved. It's about concentrating your involvement where it creates the most value. More can happen without more depending on you.

Papillon Luck

“Papillon’s superpower is delivery. It gets done, no ifs, buts or excuses, just done. Her drive coupled with extraordinary focus allows her to perform optimally and consistently.”

Simon MayDirector, Impeller Ventures

Papillon spent fourteen years in institutional finance, developing a pattern of being brought into new firms and funds at launch.

Her career began in the dealing room at GNI, a futures and options broker on LIFFE, before moving to Newton Investment Management and then Schroders, whose telecoms analysts took her with them to Credit Suisse First Boston. Ron Beller later recruited her from Goldman Sachs to help launch Peloton Partners, working alongside the Head of Investor Relations through its fundraises. Peloton raised more than $1 billion within months and reached $2.6 billion AUM within two years.

That became a recurring theme. When a founding partner left to start Stoneworks, he asked her to join him at launch. Praxient and StormHarbour later recruited her for the same reason: to help build from the beginning.

Eventually she did it for herself. Sixteen years building and directing her own consumer companies across physical product and healthtech: developing products, raising capital, answering to investors and shareholders, building the supply chain and taking a luxury jet-lag supplement range from formulation into Selfridges, NET-A-PORTER and MR PORTER.

The same travel-health proposition extended into technology. Building at the Travel Tech Lab in London & Partners, she developed an app to MVP, tested by Loughborough University athletes, alongside Fit to Fly: a concept connecting flight data, physiology and wearables into a personalised airport experience. It won the Lab’s 2017 pitch competition, run with Collinson Group.

She was also hired as right hand to Dragons’ Den investor James Caan at his private equity firm Hamilton Bradshaw, in what would now be called a Chief of Staff role. She worked across his business and investment interests, including Start Up Loans in its early days, and worked on the early Crowdcube project with its founders before the platform had launched.

People who worked with her at close range didn’t want to work without her.

Papillon has built her own businesses and operated alongside founders building theirs. That changes how she works: where she sees risk, how she weighs priorities, which constraints are real, and what genuinely needs the founder.

You get judgement shaped by building businesses, not only by operating inside them.

06 / Why fractional

Get the leverage before
you add the headcount.

A Fractional Chief of Staff isn't a smaller version of a full-time hire. It's senior operating capability, focused on you and the work that creates the most leverage.

What can you actually accomplish fractionally?

The point isn't to fill the hours. It's to improve what happens beyond them.

Part of the work is solving what's in front of you. Part is improving the workflows, decision-making and ways of working that keep things moving without constant founder input. You're buying leverage, not activity.

Can you understand my business if you're not here full-time?

Fractional doesn't mean peripheral.

WellBuilt works remotely, directly with you and across the business. That means getting inside the priorities, people, decisions and dependencies that shape the company. You don’t need someone sitting beside you five days a week. You need someone close enough to know what matters and senior enough to know what to do about it.

Will you actually own anything?

You're not buying advice. You're buying senior ownership.

That means taking work off you, driving it forward and bringing decisions back when they genuinely need you. A conversation with your Chief of Staff shouldn't leave you with more work to do.

What does working together actually look like?

Dedicated capacity, with continuity through the week.

WellBuilt works inside the business, moving priorities, decisions and execution forward while maintaining the context and continuity needed to keep work moving.

The level of support is shaped around the company’s stage, operating complexity and what needs to be owned.

What happens when something urgent comes up?

The capacity flexes around what the business needs.

Some weeks are predictable. Others aren't. The working model leaves room for decisions, follow-up and issues that can't wait until the next focused working day.

Why wouldn't I just hire a full-time Chief of Staff?

At some point, you might.

A full-time Chief of Staff makes sense when there is enough ongoing work to justify permanent headcount. But company size or funding stage doesn’t determine that need. Even a Series B scale-up may only need senior Chief of Staff capability part-time.

Fractional gives you that capability without creating a full-time role simply because the business has reached a certain stage.

07 / Who it's for

Too much of the business
still runs through you.

WellBuilt is for funded, high-growth Health and Wellness founders and CEOs who need senior operating capacity before they need another full-time executive.

This is for you if
  • Too much of the business still lands with you, even when someone else should be able to own it.
  • You want ownership and execution, not another adviser handing the work back to you.
  • You need senior capability without creating a full-time role to get it.
  • Decisions, dependencies and critical work keep finding their way back to you.
  • Important work crosses teams and functions, but no one person owns the whole picture.
  • You want automation built into how the work runs, where it creates leverage.
This isn't for you if
  • You’re looking primarily for calendar, inbox, travel or administrative support.
  • You want a consultant to produce recommendations while you implement them.
  • You need a full-time Chief of Staff working inside the business five days a week.
  • You want to hand over the decisions only you can make.
  • You need a functional leader to own one specific area rather than someone working across the gaps.
  • You want an AI automation agency or development team.

If too much of this sounds like your business, the Founder Diagnostic is where we work out where the dependency sits, and whether WellBuilt is the right way to remove it.

can still carry it all. It's whether

08 / Questions

The questions founders ask
before we work together.

How do the first 90 days work?

The first 90 days are about getting properly inside the business and taking ownership.

We learn the priorities, people, decisions and recurring work by operating alongside you. We take ownership of what keeps routing back to you and identify where founder dependency can be reduced. Ninety days is the point at which that context is real rather than theoretical.

It isn’t a trial period. It’s the time it takes for the work to start compounding.

What happens after the first 90 days?

The work compounds from there.

By 90 days, WellBuilt has the context to operate with real ownership. If we continue, the next engagement period is another 90 days.

Over those next three months, we build on that context: strengthening operating rhythms, reducing founder dependency further, and simplifying or automating recurring work where it creates leverage.

By 180 days, the aim is a business that depends less on you to keep moving, with deeper operating context allowing WellBuilt to own more of what would otherwise come back to you.

How does AI fit into the Chief of Staff work?

AI and automation are tools WellBuilt uses where they create leverage, not a separate service.

The Chief of Staff work identifies where time is being lost, work is repeating or information is moving inefficiently. Where AI or automation can improve that, we build it into how the work runs. Where it can’t, we don’t.

The goal isn’t more AI. It’s a better-run business.

How many companies does WellBuilt work with?

A deliberately limited number at any one time.

The work depends on holding real context across a business. That isn’t possible across a large client list, so capacity is capped deliberately to protect the quality and seniority of every engagement.

How quickly can we start?

If there’s capacity, we can start straight away.

If current capacity is committed, we’ll tell you on the Founder Diagnostic, let you know when the next engagement is likely to open up, and give you the option to join the waitlist.

Is the Founder Diagnostic a sales call?

It’s a working conversation about where the business still depends on you.

If a Fractional Chief of Staff isn’t the right answer, we’ll say so. Thirty minutes is enough to work out whether it is.

What does it cost?

From $6,000 every four weeks. The engagement is structured in 90-day periods.

The level of engagement reflects the company’s stage, operating complexity and the level of support required.
